visualBrief: Seoul’s Changdeokgung palace and Secret Garden. The double-roof throne hall, stepping terraces, three open court gates, blue-tiled council hall and residence wings lead across native paths to distinct garden pavilions above native streams and ponds.

photoFacing.frontBasis: Korea Heritage Service plan and photos, with each footprint fitted to PMTiles and the approach at the intersection of the Bukyeongcheon and the mapped path.

terrain: Bilinear six-meter sampling from standard zoom-15 Terrarium tiles.
limitations: Exterior reconstruction of the mapped palace courts and principal Secret Garden pavilions and Geumcheongyo’s paired stone arches. Building elevations use six-meter standard terrain samples.
Individual dancheong motifs, roof figures and carved plaques are interpreted at viewer scale. Interiors, isolated service buildings and the far northern Jade Stream are outside this reconstruction.
The bridge follows the mapped footpath. Native terrain stays in place, so channel detail below the arch openings depends on terrain resolution.
